title: Learning Hamiltonian Dynamics at Scale: A Differential-Geometric Approach
claim: A high-dimensional system is encoded to a low-dimensional symplectic submanifold, evolved with a structure-preserving geometric model, and decoded back.
layout: Bottom left-to-right pipeline, with geometry cartoon and constrained-AE inset above
description: A wide flowchart with a pipeline along the bottom. Inputs (external torque, momentum p0, position q0) enter a blue encoder panel labeled rho. They pass into a central pink-brown box labeled geometric HNN. That box holds an SPD-cone sketch with two small purple and orange networks that produce D(q) and M^-1(q). It also holds a green potential-energy network that produces V(q). Smaller boxes show the Hamiltonian, its derivatives and the vector fields. These are combined by a plus node and fed to an integral block, which is a Strang symplectic integrator. The output goes to a blue decoder panel labeled phi, which produces predicted p and q. The top left has a curved manifold with sphere images for ground truth and model predictions. The top right has a blue constrained AE inset with layer notation. Dotted arrows show secondary data flow.
caption: Flowchart of the forward dynamics of the geometric RO-HNN. The geometrically-constrained symplectic AE (in blue) is built as the cotangent lift of a constrained AE (top right). The geometric HNN (in brown) is composed of two SPD networks, one MLP, and a Strang symplectic integrator.
abstract: Embedding physical intuition into network architectures allows the learning of dynamics that enforce fundamental properties, such as energy conservation laws, thereby leading to physically-plausible predictions. Yet, scaling these models to high-dimensional dynamical systems remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces Reduced-order Hamiltonian Neural Network (RO-HNN), a novel physics-inspired neural network that combines the conservation laws of Hamiltonian mechanics with the scalability of model order reduction. RO-HNN is built on two core components: a novel geometrically-constrained symplectic autoencoder that learns a low-dimensional, structure-preserving symplectic submanifold, and a geometric Hamiltonian neural network that models the dynamics on the submanifold. Our experiments demonstrate that RO-HNN provides physically-consistent, stable, and generalizable predictions of complex high-dimensional dynamics, thereby effectively extending the scope of Hamiltonian neural networks to high-dimensional physical systems.
